Jordan / team — quick legal read and recommendation. I’ve reviewed sentinel_redlines_v3.pdf and flagged the following high-risk items: 

1) Regulatory fines indemnity: They’re asking us to indemnify for fines/penalties in EU. We cannot accept indemnity for regulatory penalties (e.g., GDPR fines) — liability here is strict, unlimited, and contractually transferring regulatory risk is company policy no-go. Recommend flat refusal; propose enhanced cooperation clause + robust DPAs and data processing terms instead.

2) Removal of gross negligence carveout: The redline deletes the gross negligence / willful misconduct exception. That is material. We should preserve carveouts for gross negligence/willful misconduct. Any removal requires exec legal sign-off and insurance review.

3) Liability cap increase to €3M / 24 months: Current playbook: one year of fees or $1M standard. For strategic deals we can consider up to $2M (or 12 months fees) with exec approval and additional mitigations (audit, SOC evidence, indemnity carve-outs). I recommend counter to €2M limited to EU jurisdiction and only for claims tied to IP/data processor obligations for 12 months post‑execution.

4) Warranty: 36 months data export guarantee is open-ended and operationally risky. Suggest limiting warranty to representations about data exportability at time of delivery and offering SLA credits for availability breaches (no long-term indemnity).

Bottom line: we should not accept regulatory fines indemnity; keep gross negligence carveout; negotiate cap to €2M (exec approval required) and narrow indemnity to IP/data breach scope. Any cap above $1M needs approval from Markus. If sales want to push higher, need insurance and CISO sign-off.

I’ll draft clean fallback language for the EU‑specific annex and a short exec memo with risk items.

– Dev
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Adding pricing perspective: current ARR run-rate for this customer is ~€420k; 36 months at 35% would reduce ROI materially. Pricing ops recommends the following trade:

- Approve a one‑time commercial concession: 20–25% TCV discount if legal accepts capped liability at €2M and indemnity limited to IP/data processor scope.
- Add 6 months of SLA credits (tiered) and an implementation professional services credit to offset warranty ask.
- Require 24‑month term and prepayment for the first 12 months to mitigate risk.

I’ve attached a pricing_workup.xlsx with scenarios. If exec insists on the €3M cap and broad indemnity, we should escalate for a strategic discount approval beyond 30% (requires CRO sign-off).

– Marissa
Head of Deal Desk Operations
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Escalation: Sentinel contract — exec decision requested (indemnity / cap / discount)

Markus — quick escalation and ask for exec sign-off. Sentinel is strategic (large AI provider, EU footprint). They’ve presented final redlines asking for: broad indemnity including regulatory fines, removal of gross negligence carveout, warranty extension, and a €3M liability cap (24 months of fees), plus 35% discount.

Legal (Dev) recommends we refuse regulatory fines indemnity, preserve gross negligence carveout, and limit liability cap to €2M (12 months of fees) if we accept narrowed indemnity to IP/data processor obligations. Pricing (Marissa) recommends 20–25% discount in exchange and prepayment/term concessions.

Proposed executive decision (requested):
- Approve narrow, EU-only indemnity limited to IP infringement and data processor obligations (no regulatory fines).
- Approve increase of liability cap to €2M (instead of €3M) for an initial 12‑month acceptance window; require re-review thereafter.
- Approve a 25% TCV discount contingent on 24‑month term and prepayment of first 12 months; include 6 months SLA credits and a one‑time implementation credit.

If approved, Legal will prepare an amendment and Risk will onboard for monitoring. If you cannot approve, recommend asking Sentinel to accept our fallback language: preserve carveouts, refuse regulatory fines indemnity, offer SLA credits in lieu of extended warranty, and cap at €1M / 12 months fees.

Attached: summary_escalation.pdf, pricing_workup.xlsx

Can you confirm by EOD tomorrow (2026-10-03)?

Thanks — Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Escalation: Sentinel contract — exec decision requested (indemnity / cap / discount)

Jordan / team — read and approve with conditions.

Decision: APPROVE the narrow EU-only indemnity limited to IP infringement and data-processor obligations (explicitly exclude regulatory fines and penalties). APPROVE liability cap increase to €2M, but limited to EU jurisdiction and for a 12‑month pilot window. After 12 months we will re-evaluate based on claim history and risk register.

Commercial concession: approve up to 22% TCV discount (not 25%) in exchange for 24‑month term and prepayment of first 12 months. Approve 4 months of SLA credits and a one‑time implementation credit. Any greater concession requires sign-off from the CRO and CFO.

Conditions before signature: 
- CISO must sign off on the risk mitigation plan and SOC2 evidence to be provided.
- Legal to draft a narrow EU annex and amendment with the exact language limits.
- Deal must be entered into Risk Register and insurance to check coverage for €2M exposure.

Dev: please prepare the amendment and a short legal memo for procurement to include in the DocuSign packet. Marissa: update pricing and procurement terms and ensure prepayment is captured. Jordan: communicate outcome to Sentinel and push for acceptance of fallback if they insist on more.

Markus
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
